Posterity

pos-TER-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Posterity is all future generations of people.

The old shipbuilder kept detailed drawings of every vessel he ever built, insisting posterity would want proof the ships were real.

Worked Example

The time capsule buried beneath the school was meant for posterity, not to be opened for another hundred years.

Posterity refers to the people who will come long after us -- our descendants and the generations beyond them.

How Posterity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

descendants

descendants: people who come after, especially one's offspring

progeny

progeny: a person's or group's offspring collectively

Antonyms

ancestors

ancestors: people from whom one is descended

forebears

forebears: ancestors or earlier generations

How Strong Is It? — successors → eternity → posterity

successors vs. posterity

successors vs. posterity: Successors are simply the specific people who take over a role or position, a narrower idea than the sweeping generations of posterity.

eternity vs. posterity

eternity vs. posterity: Eternity stretches even further than posterity, describing unending time itself rather than the generations within it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — poster-

root — poster-: coming after, later (Latin posterus)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Posterity comes from Latin posterus ('coming after, later'), the same root behind the everyday word posterior ('located behind or after'), plus -ity -- 'those who come after.'

Use the root in a new word: posterior

Root Check

Word Choice

Posterity is almost always used with a sense of legacy -- preserving, recording, or protecting something specifically so that people not yet born will benefit from it.
